worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=27,$ $r=\frac{1}{3}$ and $N=5.$ If we substitute these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}27{(\frac{1}{3})}^{n-1} & =27\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{5}]}{(1-\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =27\cdot \frac{[1-\frac{1}{243}]}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =27\cdot \frac{(\frac{242}{243})}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =27\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{242}{243} \\  & =\frac{121}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
